evidence: This is supported by data from smFISH experiments.

claim: The failure to incorporate the full complement of germline determinants is responsible at least in part for the PGC phenotypes observed in the zld and clamp RNA knockdowns.
source: The failure to incorporate the full complement of germline determinants is responsible at least in part for the PGC phenotypes observed in the zld and clamp RNA knockdowns.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed phenotypes and prior knowledge.

claim: Similar PGC phenotypes are observed in gcl mutants and in mutants in components of the BMP signaling pathway.
source: Consistent with this conclusion, similar PGC phenotypes are observed in gcl mutants and in mutants in components of the BMP signaling pathway (Colonnetta et al., 2021b; Colonnetta et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research by the authors.

claim: In gcl mutants and in mutants in components of the BMP signaling pathway, germline determinants are not efficiently captured by the cellularizing PGCs.
source: In both of these cases, germline determinants are not efficiently captured by the cellularizing PGCs.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research by the authors.

claim: The ectopic presence of germline determinants in a somatic domain is likely responsible for exacerbating the reductions in transcription of tll and dpp in the posterior soma of zldi1m knockdown embryos.
source: Likewise, the ectopic presence of germline determinants in a somatic domain is likely responsible for exacerbating the reductions in transcription of tll and dpp in the posterior soma of zldi1m knockdown embryos.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed phenotypes and prior knowledge.

claim: pgc, gcl, and nos can downregulate transcription in the soma upon overexpression or ectopic expression.
source: This is supported by earlier observations showing that pgc, gcl, and nos can downregulate transcription in the soma upon overexpression or ectopic expression (de Las Heras et al., 2009; Deshpande et al., 2005; Robertson et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: There are likely many other genes that are active in the posterior region of blastoderm stage embryos whose expression is downregulated not only because of the loss of zld, but also because of the inappropriate localization of germ plasm away from the posterior cortex.
source: Likely there are many other genes that are active in the posterior region of blastoderm stage embryos whose expression is downregulated not only because of the loss of zld, but also because of the inappropriate localization of germ plasm away from the posterior cortex.
evidence: This is speculation based on the observed effects on tll and dpp.

claim: The likely primary cause of germline/soma phenotypes—the failure to capture the germline determinants during PGC cellularization—happens during NC9/10 (if not before).
source: While many of these germline/soma phenotypes manifest themselves most clearly toward the end of the syncytial blastoderm stage or beginning of cellularization (NC13 and NC14, respectively), the likely primary cause—the failure to capture the germline determinants during PGC cellularization—happens earlier during NC9/10 (if not before).
evidence: This is an inference based on the timing of PGC cellularization.

claim: ZGA-dependent functions that take place during the minor wave are important for proper PGC cellularization whereby the germline determinants are efficiently sequestered.
source: Since this is prior to the major wave, it would suggest that ZGA-dependent functions that take place during the minor wave are important for proper PGC cellularization whereby the germline determinants are efficiently sequestered.
evidence: This is an inference based on the timing of the phenotypes.

claim: Most of the phenotypic consequences induced by loss of either Zld or CLAMP proteins can be correlated with dysregulation of centrosome function which is essential for proper PGC determination.
source: Most of the phenotypic consequences induced by loss of either Zld or CLAMP proteins can be correlated with dysregulation of centrosome function which is essential for proper PGC determination (Raff and Glover, 1989; Lerit and Gavis, 2011; Lerit et al., 2017; Colonnetta et al., 2021a).
evidence: This is supported by data showing centrosome defects and citations to prior research.

claim: Disruptions in centrosome functions not only cause defects in PGC cellularization, but also lead to the inefficient incorporation of germline determinants into PGCs when they cellularize.
source: Previous studies have shown that disruptions in centrosome functions not only cause defects in PGC cellularization, but also lead to the inefficient incorporation of germline determinants into PGCs when they cellularize (Lerit et al., 2017; Colonnetta et al., 2021b).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: One plausible idea is that the centrosomal defects in RNAi knockdown embryos are due to the disruption of some critical chromosomal function of the ZGA regulators.
source: One plausible idea is that the centrosomal defects in RNAi knockdown embryos are due to the disruption of some critical chromosomal function of the ZGA regulators.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism underlying the centrosome defects.

claim: The probable culprit for centrosome defects is the striking and pervasive defects in the nuclear division cycles.
source: In this model, the probable culprit is the striking and pervasive defects in the nuclear division cycles.
evidence: This is speculation based on the observed nuclear division defects.

claim: Nuclear division defects are already evident in zldi1m embryos in NC7-9 in the period leading up to the formation of pole buds.
source: Nuclear division defects are already evident in zldi1m embryos in NC7-9 in the period leading up to the formation of pole buds.
evidence: This is supported by data from immunostaining experiments.

claim: Zld and CLAMP are thought to participate in the remodeling of chromatin, generating regions of DNA that are nucleosome free and accessible for interactions with a variety of DNA binding proteins that have functions not directly related to transcription.
source: Like GAF (Tsukiyama et al., 1994; Wall et al., 1995), Zld and CLAMP are thought to participate in the remodeling of chromatin, generating regions of DNA that are nucleosome free and accessible for interactions with a variety of DNA binding proteins that have functions not directly related to transcription.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge of chromatin remodeling factors and citations to prior research.

claim: DNA binding proteins that interact with nucleosome-free regions include components of the origin recognition complex (ORC) and topoisomerase II.
source: These would include components of the origin recognition complex (ORC) and topoisomerase II.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge of DNA replication and chromosome structure.

claim: ORC is responsible for generating the closely spaced replication origins that are essential for completing DNA synthesis in minutes rather hours during the rapid nuclear division cycles.
source: The former is responsible for generating the closely spaced replication origins that are essential for completing DNA synthesis in minutes rather hours during the rapid nuclear division cycles.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge of DNA replication.

claim: If ORC cannot gain access to the normal complement of replication origins in early embryos, replication will not be completed in time for nuclear division.
source: If ORC cannot gain access to the normal complement of replication origins in early embryos, replication will not be completed in time for nuclear division (Miotto et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an inference based on the role of ORC and supported by citation.

claim: Topoisomerase II functions in decatenating chromosomes after replication is complete.
source: The latter, topoisomerase II, functions in decatenating chromosomes after replication is complete (Nielsen et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Topoisomerase II requires open regions of chromatin in order to access the DNA.
source: Like many other proteins that interact with DNA, topoisomerase II requires open regions of chromatin in order to access the DNA (Sperling et al., 2011; Udvardy and Schedl, 1991).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Reduction in DNA accessibility in zld or clamp RNAi knockdown embryos would be expected to impact decatenation.
source: For this reason, reduction in DNA accessibility in zld or clamp RNAi knockdown embryos would be expected to impact decatenation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the role of Zld and CLAMP in chromatin accessibility.

claim: If mitosis proceeds without completing replication and/or decatenation, chromosomes would be expected to fragment.
source: If mitosis proceeds without completing replication and/or decatenation, chromosomes would be expected to fragment, as is observed.
evidence: This is an inference based on the consequences of incomplete replication or decatenation.

claim: Chromosome fragmentation could lead to deficiencies in centrosome function, including assembly, duplication, and separation.
source: This could, in turn, lead to deficiencies in centrosome function, including assembly, duplication, and separation.
evidence: This is speculation about the consequences of chromosome fragmentation.

claim: Centrosomal defects would be expected to interfere with the efficient incorporation of germline determinants into PGCs as they cellularize.
source: These centrosomal defects would be expected to interfere with the efficient incorporation of germline determinants into PGCs as they cellularize (Lerit et al., 2017; Lerit and Gavis, 2011; Raff and Glover, 1989).
evidence: This is an inference based on the role of centrosomes in PGC formation and supported by citations.

claim: It is possible that centrosomal defects could trigger the aberrant release and spreading of germ plasm constituents that is observed in zldi1m knockdown embryos.
source: It is also possible that they could trigger the aberrant release and spreading of germ plasm constituents that is observed in zldi1m knockdown embryos.
evidence: This is speculation about the consequences of centrosome defects.

claim: It is not clear whether the early mitotic defects observed in embryos compromised for zelda activity can be tied directly to the failure to establish a sufficient number of nucleosome-free regions or an early deficit in global transcription.
source: At this point, it is not clear whether the early mitotic defects observed in embryos compromised for zelda activity (Staudt et al., 2006, this study) can be tied directly to the failure to establish a sufficient number of nucleosome-free regions or an early deficit in global transcription.
evidence: This acknowledges uncertainty about the mechanism.

claim: Some authors have suggested that transcription in pre-syncytial embryos may be needed to prepare the genome for ZGA.
source: Some authors have suggested that transcription in pre-syncytial embryos may be needed to prepare the genome for ZGA (Ali-Murthy et al., 2013; Harrison et al., 2010), and there could be a similar requirement for the functioning of factors that are important for replication and mitosis.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

source: Some authors have suggested that transcription in pre-syncytial embryos may be needed to prepare the genome for ZGA (Ali-Murthy et al., 2013; Harrison et al., 2010), and there could be a similar requirement for the functioning of factors that are important for replication and mitosis.
evidence: This is speculation based on prior suggestions about the role of early transcription.

source: An alternative (or additional) model is that one or more genes expressed during the minor wave could be important in directing the process of PGC cellularization and normal centrosome function.
evidence: This is speculation about an alternative mechanism.

claim: PGC formation and proper specification in early embryos depends upon zygotic activity of the BMP pathway.
source: This is a plausible mechanism as previous studies have shown that PGC formation and proper specification in early embryos depends upon zygotic activity of the BMP pathway (Colonnetta et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research by the authors.

source: For example, when dpp expression is inhibited by zygotic RNAi knockdown, germline determinants like gcl and pgc mRNAs are not fully captured by the PGCs when they cellularize.

claim: The BMP pathway is not the only possible transcriptional target that could affect PGC formation.
source: The BMP pathway is not the only possible transcriptional target.

source: The expression of factors that have a direct role in the assembly or functioning of centrosomes might also be downregulated in zld and clamp RNAi knockdown embryos.

claim: These observations document unprecedented activities of ZGA pioneer factors, Zld and CLAMP.
source: In sum, together these observations document unprecedented activities of ZGA pioneer factors, Zld and CLAMP.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the study's significance.

source: Our data show that the lineage potential of embryonic nuclei is gradually restricted via the combined action of ZGA components as these proteins influence acquisition of either somatic or germline identity during early syncytial blastoderm stages.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the data presented in the study.

source: Thus far, germline identity is thought to be solely determined by Oskar-dependent assembly of germline specific proteins and RNAs.
evidence: This is a statement of the traditional view based on established knowledge.

source: Somatic fate, by contrast, can be essentially viewed as a 'default' state that depends on the absence of germline determinants.

source: Our data argue that ZGA, a process that confers specific fate on individual somatic cells, initially guards their somatic identity.
